artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime, and for a subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ define the Fourier transform
$$\widehat{A}(z) = \sum_{a \in A} e^{2\pi i a z / p}, \qquad z \in \mathbb{F}_p.$$
A three-term arithmetic progression in $A$ is a triple $(x, x+d, x+2d) \in A^3$ with $d \ne 0$.

Question: Is it true that for every pair of fixed constants $C, D > 0$ there exists $p_0 = p_0(C,D)$ such that for every prime $p \ge p_0$, any set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ satisfying
$$|A| > \frac{p}{\log^C p} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \sum_{z \in \mathbb{F}_p} |\widehat{A}(z)| < p \log^D p$$
must contain a non-trivial three-term arithmetic progression?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific question was located. It is posed as an open problem in the additive combinatorics community concerning whether small Fourier L1-norm forces 3APs in dense subsets of F_p, and standard surveys on Roth-type theorems do not report a proof.

status_evidence.title: Forbidding 3-Term Arithmetic Progressions (MIT OCW lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes on Roth's theorem and Fourier-analytic methods for 3APs, with no mention of a resolution of the L1-Fourier-norm version of the problem.
status_evidence.claim: Recent expository sources on 3AP problems do not record this question as solved.
